beats.say: A penny gets you a library. And it never stops.
Choose eight albums for a penny, then you're a member.
Pick a regular-price album each month, no deadline to decline.
Let the next selection auto-ship unless you cancel in time.
Revenue dropped from $1.4 billion in 1996 to $17 million in 2014. Sounds generous.
But it does a job: the penny is a loss leader.
The auto-ship clause forces purchases each cycle, turning the penny into a hidden bill.
Peak revenue hit $1.4 billion in 1996, then collapsed.
You see it everywhere. A gym offers a $1 entry, then a $30 monthly fee.
A streaming app gives a free month, then $9.99 unless you cancel.
Because the cheap entry forces recurring payments, the pricier plan feels like the smart choice.
A tiny upfront cost can mask ongoing charges. Follow for more.
